To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we investigated the activation of Nrf2 and AhR and their interactions in toxicogenomic databases and that we developed a bioinformatic approach that allows to classify compounds by their potency and their specificity in activating Nrf2, or AhR or both.
we have identified and characterized the transcriptional activation signatures of three key transcription factors, Nrf2, ATF4 and AhR.

1) the AhR and the Nrf2 pathways are activated by different chemicals and with different kinetics, 2) the ATF4 pathway is activated by different chemicals than the AhR and Nrf2 pathways and with different kinetics and 3) the AhR pathway is more selective in its activation than the Nrf2 and the ATF4 pathways.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the signature of each pathway, with the definition of a chemical activation capacity score and with the identification of a set of chemicals activating each pathway.
the identification of the transcription factors involved in the regulation of the expression of the genes in the toxicogenomic datasets and with the identification of their signature.

the investigation of the activation of transcriptional stress response pathways in toxicogenomic datasets and with the development of a bioinformatic approach to refine the pathways' signature, to classify chemicals according to their activation potency and to identify potential biological read across on the basis of the activation of a given transcriptional pathway.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the AhR, Nrf2 and ATF4 pathways are not completely independent and that the activation of one of them may be associated with the activation of one or two others.
the AhR pathway is the most activated transcription factor in toxicogenomics studies, followed by the Nrf2 and the ATF4 pathways.
Nrf2 and ATF4 pathways are highly overlapping and that the AhR pathway is independent of the other two.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the AhR and Nrf2 pathways are more conserved across species than the ATF4 pathway, and that the AhR pathway is the one that is the most conserved across cell models.
the three pathways we studied are distinct, but partially overlapping and that the AhR pathway is the most sensitive and the most specific.
we have developed a novel approach to identify and classify the chemicals based on their potency and selectivitiy to activate the three pathways.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the three transcription factors are activated by distinct sets of chemicals and are activated to different extents by the same chemicals.
the AhR and the ATF4 pathways are highly conserved between human and rat, while the Nrf2 signature is highly divergent.
the AhR pathway is the most activated pathway in the datasets, followed by the ATF4 and Nrf2 pathways.
